original_question: If G is a connected n-vertex m-edge graph minimizing lambda(G) - d(G) among all connected graphs with those parameters, must the degree spread satisfy Delta(G) - delta(G) <= 1?
target_in_paper: Section 11, "Graphs with a prescribed average degree," Problem 5 (Hong [3]): for fixed n and m, with H(n,m) the set of connected graphs on n vertices and m edges, if G ∈ H(n,m) minimizes λ(G) − d(G), ask whether Δ(G) − δ(G) ≤ 1. ([ort.shu.edu.cn](https://www.ort.shu.edu.cn/CN/article/downloadArticleFile.do?attachType=PDF&id=20117&utm_source=openai))
correct_elements: Your draft already identifies the right extremal setup (connected graphs with fixed n and m), the right objective function (λ(G) − d(G)), and the right conclusion (Δ(G) − δ(G) ≤ 1). That is exactly the content of Hong’s Problem 5 once the paper’s notation is restored. ([ort.shu.edu.cn](https://www.ort.shu.edu.cn/CN/article/downloadArticleFile.do?attachType=PDF&id=20117&utm_source=openai))
missing_details: The paper packages the ambient family as H(n,m), the set of connected graphs on n vertices and m edges; the introduction also assumes throughout that graphs are simple, undirected, and unweighted. ([ort.shu.edu.cn](https://www.ort.shu.edu.cn/CN/article/downloadArticleFile.do?attachType=PDF&id=20117&utm_source=openai))

λ(G) should be identified explicitly as λ1(G), the largest eigenvalue of the adjacency matrix A(G), i.e. the adjacency spectral radius. ([ort.shu.edu.cn](https://www.ort.shu.edu.cn/CN/article/downloadArticleFile.do?attachType=PDF&id=20117&utm_source=openai))

d(G) should be defined explicitly as the average degree of G; in H(n,m), this equals 2m/n. The paragraph immediately after Problem 5 uses this notation in exactly that way. ([ort.shu.edu.cn](https://www.ort.shu.edu.cn/CN/article/downloadArticleFile.do?attachType=PDF&id=20117&utm_source=openai))

The quantifiers should be made stand-alone: fix integers n and m with H(n,m) nonempty, and let G range over H(n,m). The draft leaves this implicit. ([ort.shu.edu.cn](https://www.ort.shu.edu.cn/CN/article/downloadArticleFile.do?attachType=PDF&id=20117&utm_source=openai))

Δ(G) and δ(G) should be defined explicitly as the maximum and minimum degrees, respectively. ([ort.shu.edu.cn](https://www.ort.shu.edu.cn/CN/article/downloadArticleFile.do?attachType=PDF&id=20117&utm_source=openai))
refined_question: Fix integers n and m with H(n,m) nonempty, where H(n,m) denotes the family of connected simple undirected unweighted graphs on n vertices and m edges. If G ∈ H(n,m) minimizes λ(G) − d(G), where λ(G) = λ1(G) is the largest eigenvalue of the adjacency matrix of G and d(G) = 2m/n is the average degree of G, must G satisfy Δ(G) − δ(G) ≤ 1? ([ort.shu.edu.cn](https://www.ort.shu.edu.cn/CN/article/downloadArticleFile.do?attachType=PDF&id=20117&utm_source=openai))
justification: This is the exact target because Section 11 first defines H(n,m) and says that the section studies connected n-vertex m-edge graphs of minimum spectral radius, and then immediately states Hong’s Problem 5 in the λ(G) − d(G) form with the conclusion Δ(G) − δ(G) ≤ 1. The notation paragraph on page 34 supplies the meanings of λ(G), d(G), Δ(G), and δ(G). I therefore kept your question narrow and paper-faithful, changing only what was needed to make it self-contained. Since d(G) = 2m/n is fixed on H(n,m), your draft is effectively aligned with the section’s minimum-spectral-radius viewpoint, but the paper’s nearest official formulation is the λ(G) − d(G) version in Problem 5. ([ort.shu.edu.cn](https://www.ort.shu.edu.cn/CN/article/downloadArticleFile.do?attachType=PDF&id=20117&utm_source=openai))
